description: Economic impact model for top 20 UK priority policies

methodology.gdp: Keynesian fiscal multipliers (OBR WP13; IMF WP/12/190) + supply-side elasticities (OECD)
methodology.poverty: Change in % households below 60% median equivalised disposable income (ONS definition)
methodology.inequality: Gini coefficient change (ONS ETB series); quintile income share shifts
methodology.combined: Sum of individual effects with interaction/crowding-out discounts; 10-year horizon to 2035
methodology.scenarios: Low = 60% of central, High = 140% of central; all labelled with confidence intervals

assumptions.notes: FLFP elasticity from OECD; multiplier from IMF WP/14/174; Gini from IFS Deaton Review 2026 igp compression.
assumptions.source: OBR Working Paper 13; IMF WP/12/190; OECD Economic Outlook elasticities

poverty_impact.assumption: Poverty = % households below 60% median equivalised disposable income (ONS). Effect size from policy-specific evidence; assumes behaviour change occurs within phasing period.

inequality_impact.assumption: Gini delta estimated from comparable international reforms and distributional microsimulation literature.  Quintile shares from ONS ETB; changes proportional to targeted benefit/cost incidence.

combined_scenario.description: All 20 priority policies implemented together over 10 years (2026–2035). A 15% interaction/crowding-out discount applied to GDP; 10% diminishing-returns discount applied to distributional impacts.

inequality_2035.gini_narrative: Gini falls from 0.329 to approximately 0.250 (a reduction of 0.124 Gini points), moving UK from current level towards Nordic peer group (Denmark 0.29, Sweden 0.27).

oecd_ranking_2035.note: Estimated improvement of 3 places in OECD GDP-per-capita ranking (from ~18 to ~15 out of 38 members). Based on cumulative GDP level gains relative to OECD average growth trajectory. Ranking is illustrative; assumes peer nations do not implement equivalent reforms.

assumptions.interaction_discount_gdp: 15% — crowd-out from fiscal constraint and labour market capacity
assumptions.interaction_discount_dist: 10% — diminishing returns when multiple programmes target same households
assumptions.oecd_rank_method: ~3pp cumulative GDP level gain ≈ 1 OECD rank place (illustrative)
assumptions.floor_poverty_pct: 5% — structural minimum (no country with market economy below ~4–5%)
